raw.description:
About AIOS

AIOS is building the world’s first full-stack AI doctor.

We’re at $450M ARR, growing from $7M/yr in April 2025. We’re faithfully serving 200k/mo patients via Bolt Pharmacy, our main UK brand. We’ve just launched Bolt Med, our international brand. We’re profitable.

Our strategy exists at the intersection of two strong theses:

  1. The AI doctor that wins will get to escape velocity using GLP-1s, the fastest growing consumer product in history.

  2. The $2T European healthcare market is overlooked by the most talented builders.

Our master plan:

  • Step 0 → $100M/yr by end of 2025: We went from $10M to $100M in 6 months serving the UK GLP-1 market.

  • Step 1 → $1B ARR by end of 2026: Since April 2025 we've grown from 3k to 200k UK active GLP-1 patients. We’ll continue this growth curve to hit $1B ARR.

  • Step 2 → $10B ARR by end of 2028: Blitzscale Europe. We’ll be Europe’s largest GLP-1 provider.

  • Step 3 → $100B/yr by end of 2030: Get regulatory approval across Europe for our Full Autonomous Prescribing (FAP) system. Win contracts at scale with European payers to mass replace human labor. We’ll be the dominant full-stack AI doctor in Europe.

  • Step 4 → $1T/yr by end of 2035: With one line of code and zero human time, you can use AIOS to treat any patient globally with any medication.

In so doing, we’ll become the world’s first trillion-dollar healthcare company.

We’re a young, founder-led company. This is still Day 1 and all our work is ahead of us.

You can read more about working with us here: Working at AIOS

 

Being a Clinical Ops Lead at AIOS

We’re building a world-class team.

As Clinical Ops Lead at AIOS Tech, you’ll build an A+ clinical operations team at scale. You’ll also be our CQC Registered Manager, personally accountable for the safety and quality of our regulated service.

You’ll:

  • Lead a fast-growing UK clinical ops team. Set the bar high and make sure your team holds it.

  • Be our CQC Registered Manager. We’re inspection-ready every day, and you build the systems that keep us there.

  • Nail capacity planning. No backlogs, no long waits, no clunky patient experiences.

  • Build an operation that runs itself. Clear KPIs and SLAs, and performance management that’s automated first, so it scales as we grow.

You’re a killer operator first. You run on numbers, cadence and relentless follow-through. You spot problems before they show up in the data, fix them at the root and make sure they don’t come back. To you, the best-run operation is also the safest and most compliant one.

Our patients deserve a world-class experience. You use technology to close gaps, keep standards high and redesign pathways around what’s best for patients.

You’re not pretentious. You’ll get stuck in with the leads who report to you and make sure our strategy holds up as we scale. You’ll work with our Talent team to hire and keep the sharpest people in the country.

Doing this well means we become the UK’s largest GLP-1 provider and expand into new verticals, safely, compliantly and without slowing down.

This is a full-time, fully remote role in the UK, with occasional travel to Bolt Pharmacy in Blackburn. You’ll have flex in your calendar for kids if you have them — many of our team have kids so we’re kid-friendly.

This is a Lead role. You’ll report directly to our Head of Clinical Product & NI, Farah Haque. We’re intense, so you’ll also be intense.

You’ll also work closely with:

  • Arvee Sese-Bondoc, Customer Support Lead

  • Phuong Nguyen, Superintendent Pharmacist

  • Rich Hannibal, Head of Customer Experience & Operations

  • Zoe Wheeler, UK People Lead

 

Key responsibilities

  • Registered Manager: You’re our CQC Registered Manager and personally accountable for safe, high-quality care. You own our relationship with the CQC, set our compliance strategy and make sure the business meets the fundamental standards as it scales.

  • Quality: Working with the NI, you set our path to an Outstanding rating. You build a service that runs to the CQC’s five key questions by default, so we’re inspection-ready every day.

  • Governance: You design and lead our governance framework for incidents, complaints, safeguarding and duty of candour. You make sure the lessons drive real change in how we work to keep patients safe.

  • Leadership: You lead the leaders. You set the performance bar, and build a strong bench of team leads who maintain high standards across the entire clinical operation.

  • Talent: You’ll partner with Talent to hire and keep A+ prescribers and Team Leads. You’ll have ongoing training in place as we expand into new verticals.

  • Operational strategy: You own capacity and workforce planning in step with growth and expansion. You make the calls on structure, resourcing and investment, so demand never outpaces us.

  • Performance: You set the KPIs and SLAs the operation runs on, and hold your leads to them. You objectively assess accurate data, and are responsible for the accuracy of that data.

  • Collaboration: You’re a senior voice in the leadership team. You bring clinical ops insight into company decisions and represent the service internally and externally.

 

Need to have

  • Experience: You have 3+ years leading teams in a high-growth, digital/telehealth organization.

  • CQC: You have experience as a CQC Registered Manager, and have taken a service through a CQC inspection and received rating Good or Outstanding.

  • Alignment: You have experience leading large clinical teams (>50), and you’ve likely led teams much larger than that (>100). You smoothly get large teams aligned so everyone’s adhering to protocols and SOPs.

  • Operator: You’re a killer operator, with a track record of running clinical operations based on metrics (SLAs, rotas, forecasting). You embrace accountability, and your reports do, too.

  • Metrics: You possess data fluency and understand the importance of accurate data when it comes to setting KPIs. You have owned critical KPIs in the past and don’t balk at the responsibility that comes with it.

  • Automation: You recognize that we’re in the midst of a technological revolution, and embrace AI and automation to kill off manual, clunky workflows. You ensure your team isn’t getting left behind.

  • Standards: You maintain exceptionally high standards, a bias to action and are happy to get stuck in. You detest pretentiousness.

Nice to have

  • Product & Engineering: You’ve worked with Product and Engineering to automate operational workflows in a start-up environment. You understand what they need and don’t make vague requests without clear justification. You validate what’s shipped yourself.

  • Scale: You’ve scaled a service through rapid growth and probably launched new clinical services or verticals along the way. You can “figure it out” as you go without needing your hand held.

  • Regulatory: You possess experience with regulators and standards beyond just the CQC, such as the GPhC, MHRA, ICO and/or DSPT

 

Our cultural standards

We aim to make this your life's work. This should be the most challenging, most rewarding role of your life. Accordingly, these are the core cultural standards to which we hold ourselves & our team-members:

  1. Belief in the mission: We will have served 100 million patients by the end of 2030 and we transform the life of most patients who join. We have a lot of work to do. We are obsessed with our patients and are dedicated to the mission.

  2. Unwavering integrity: We are at the frontier, so we often live in ambiguity with no trodden path. When we can't look to others for guidance, we must maintain impeccable ethics and unwavering integrity.

  3. Only the paranoid survive: Bad sh*t is coming. By joining us, you're choosing to sail straight towards the storms with unhesitating conviction. However much we've already done, however far we've already come, it's still Day 1 and all our work is ahead of us.

  4. If we're average we fail: We are only interested in "insanely great", a focus on the quality of our execution that in everyday life would be considered pathological. We have a dedication to excellence and reject incompetence.

  5. Commitment to candor: That which can be destroyed by the truth should be. You get full transparency from the company and the company expects full transparency from you. We never say anything about someone that we wouldn't say to them directly. We give feedback with love and do not need to protect people from fleeting physical sensations.

  6. A maniacal sense of urgency: We execute at an intensity that most people think is impossible. Speed is critical and we need things done yesterday. We all work very hard and in such a competitive world there really is no other way to win.

  7. Enduring frugality: We are frugal. We hate being wasteful and we are anti-luxury. A culture of cheapness keeps us young. We spend our cash wisely & carefully, in a way that would make our grandmas proud.

  8. Bulldozing barriers: The world is malleable and we shape it. We truly believe this and act accordingly. We are relentlessly resourceful and are at the mercy of no-one but ourselves. You'll be shocked how capable you are and how much you can achieve.

  9. Keep your head down: We're boring people doing exciting work. We don't chase short-term status. We ignore short-term dopamine hits and focus on what matters. Outsiders will underestimate us and we revel in that.

  10. The power of focus: We live in a world of power laws and we cannot overestimate the unimportance of practically everything. Know your One Thing, and nail it.

🎯 "You just build a f*ing amazing experience. Make each step amazing. Make every decision in the long term interest of the customer. Give the customer massively more value than you take."

 

Compensation & Benefits

You get paid above market salary and you get early stage equity, so you get really rich if we nail this.

  • Compensation: £90k–£150k/yr inc equity

Benefits

The stuff below is cool as well.

  • Healthcare: comprehensive medical insurance (if appropriate).

  • Remote: our team is fully distributed across the world and functions fully remotely.

  • Personal development: £1,000/yr budget for books, courses, coaching.

  • Personal wellness: £1,000/yr budget for gym, health apps.

  • GLP-1s: free membership with a clinic offering GLP-1s.

  • Health coaching: free biweekly health coaching so you stay healthy.

  • Work coaching: free biweekly work coaching so you stay sharp + calm.

  • Equipment: Macbook & work-from-home equipment provided as needed.

  • What are we missing? We're still early so you get to shape our culture.

title: Staff Product Designer
description: Why Faculty? We established Faculty in 2014 because we thought that AI would be the most important technology of our time. Since then, we’ve worked with over 350 global customers to transform their performance through human-centric AI. You can read about our real-world impact here . We don’t chase hype cycles. We innovate, build and deploy responsible AI which moves the needle - and we know a thing or two about doing it well. We bring an unparalleled depth of technical, product and delivery expertise to our clients who span government, finance, retail, energy, life sciences and defence. Our business, and reputation, is growing fast and we’re always on the lookout for individuals who share our intellectual curiosity and desire to build a positive legacy through technology. AI is an epoch-defining technology, join a company where you’ll be empowered to envision its most powerful applications, and to make them happen. About Frontier Faculty Frontier™ is a decision operating system. It puts AI to work on the decisions that matter most to large organisations, such as where to invest, how to allocate resources, and when to act. Every enterprise is investing heavily in AI, but few are confident it will improve performance. Too often it goes to what’s easy to automate, disconnected from the decisions that actually move the business. Frontier works backwards from objectives like revenue, margin and risk to the decisions that drive them, then connects the data, models and agents those decisions need into a world model of the business. Teams simulate and optimise options with ADA, our AI decision agent, and every decision is tracked against its outcome so the system keeps learning. Our ambition is to make business decisions as easy to navigate as getting around a city. We don’t believe in AI that thinks for people. We believe in AI that helps people think, with humans and agents working together inside a decision system. Customers start with one high-value decision and prove value in weeks. Over months they connect it into a wider decision network, and over years they build an adaptive enterprise. Frontier is built by Faculty, an AI company that has delivered more than 400 systems since 2014 and is now part of Accenture. About Design at Frontier We’re a small team, growing deliberately - we’d rather have five designers who trust each other than fifteen who don't. We're tightly integrated with engineering. We prototype in code. We co-own the design system with developers. We're actively exploring what agentic-augmented design work looks like in practice, not in think pieces — and we're honest when we don't have the answer yet. We’re active in shaping the product culture at Frontier; putting people first, raising the quality bar and ensuring a coherent experience. You’ll be part of shaping that culture. About the role You'll be one of the most senior designers on Frontier, shaping a product that's still early enough that the decisions you make will define how it works for years. Day to day, you'll be designing the surfaces where people and agents collaborate on real clinical decisions — how evidence gets surfaced, how recommendations get explained, how humans push back, how teams learn. This is hard, unsolved design work. The existing patterns for AI interfaces mostly come from consumer chat products; they don't transfer cleanly to environments where the cost of a bad decision is measured in years of research or patient outcomes. You'll be expected to work end-to-end: from framing the problem with product and engineering, through prototyping in code and design canvases, through shipping. You'll help set the craft bar for the team, mentor the designers around you, and push back when something isn't good enough yet. What you'll work on Designing the core interaction patterns for how humans and agents collaborate inside a decision loop. Making dense, analytical information legible for expert users who need to trust it, challenge it, and act on it. Shaping the shared design language and system that lets a small team move quickly without the product fragmenting. Partnering with engineering from day one of any problem, not from handoff. Raising the bar for craft — through your own work, through critique, and through the standards you hold the team to. We think you'll do well here if You've shipped complex software for expert users, in a domain where getting it wrong has real consequences. You design end-to-end and care about the pixels as much as the strategy. You've done serious work on AI or other non-deterministic systems and have opinions about what works and what doesn't. You're comfortable prototyping in code, or motivated to get there. You're direct, kind, and can hold a clear point of view without needing to be the loudest in the room. You want the people who use your product to have better working lives because of it. You might not enjoy this role if You want to work on a mature product with established patterns. Frontier is early, and the ambiguity is real. You prefer to work handoff-style, away from engineers. You're looking for a role where design sets direction in isolation from product and engineering. We work as one team. Interview process Intro call with our talent team (30 min) Conversation with Duncan, VP of Design (60 min) Portfolio and case study deep-dive (90 min) Final conversation with a cross-functional leader (60 min) Our Recruitment Ethos We aim to grow the best team - not the most similar one. We know that diversity of individuals fosters diversity of thought, and that strengthens our principle of seeking truth. And we know from experience that diverse teams deliver better work, relevant to the world in which we live. We’re united by a deep intellectual curiosity and desire to use our abilities for measurable positive impact. We strongly encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, ethnicities, genders, religions and sexual orientations. If you don’t feel you meet all the requirements, but are excited by the role and know you bring some key strengths, please don't hesitate in applying as you might be right for this role, or other roles. We are open to conversations about part-time hours. A note on AI: we're happy for you to use it for research and interview prep, but please don't use it to generate answers during live interviews. We also use an AI note-taker (Metaview) in interviews so interviewers can stay present (which you can opt out of just let us know,) and every application is reviewed by a human, never decided by AI. Why Faculty?


We established Faculty in 2014 because we thought that AI would be the most important technology of our time. Since then, we’ve worked with over 350 global customers to transform their performance through human-centric AI. You can read about our real-world impact here.

We don’t chase hype cycles. We innovate, build and deploy responsible AI which moves the needle - and we know a thing or two about doing it well. We bring an unparalleled depth of technical, product and delivery expertise to our clients who span government, finance, retail, energy, life sciences and defence.

Our business, and reputation, is growing fast and we’re always on the lookout for individuals who share our intellectual curiosity and desire to build a positive legacy through technology.

AI is an epoch-defining technology, join a company where you’ll be empowered to envision its most powerful applications, and to make them happen.

About Frontier

Faculty Frontier™ is a decision operating system. It puts AI to work on the decisions that matter most to large organisations, such as where to invest, how to allocate resources, and when to act.

Every enterprise is investing heavily in AI, but few are confident it will improve performance. Too often it goes to what’s easy to automate, disconnected from the decisions that actually move the business.

Frontier works backwards from objectives like revenue, margin and risk to the decisions that drive them, then connects the data, models and agents those decisions need into a world model of the business. Teams simulate and optimise options with ADA, our AI decision agent, and every decision is tracked against its outcome so the system keeps learning. Our ambition is to make business decisions as easy to navigate as getting around a city.

We don’t believe in AI that thinks for people. We believe in AI that helps people think, with humans and agents working together inside a decision system.

Customers start with one high-value decision and prove value in weeks. Over months they connect it into a wider decision network, and over years they build an adaptive enterprise.

Frontier is built by Faculty, an AI company that has delivered more than 400 systems since 2014 and is now part of Accenture.

About Design at Frontier

We’re a small team, growing deliberately - we’d rather have five designers who trust each other than fifteen who don't.

We're tightly integrated with engineering. We prototype in code. We co-own the design system with developers. We're actively exploring what agentic-augmented design work looks like in practice, not in think pieces — and we're honest when we don't have the answer yet.

We’re active in shaping the product culture at Frontier; putting people first, raising the quality bar and ensuring a coherent experience. You’ll be part of shaping that culture.

About the role

You'll be one of the most senior designers on Frontier, shaping a product that's still early enough that the decisions you make will define how it works for years.

Day to day, you'll be designing the surfaces where people and agents collaborate on real clinical decisions — how evidence gets surfaced, how recommendations get explained, how humans push back, how teams learn. This is hard, unsolved design work. The existing patterns for AI interfaces mostly come from consumer chat products; they don't transfer cleanly to environments where the cost of a bad decision is measured in years of research or patient outcomes.

You'll be expected to work end-to-end: from framing the problem with product and engineering, through prototyping in code and design canvases, through shipping. You'll help set the craft bar for the team, mentor the designers around you, and push back when something isn't good enough yet.

What you'll work on

  • Designing the core interaction patterns for how humans and agents collaborate inside a decision loop.

  • Making dense, analytical information legible for expert users who need to trust it, challenge it, and act on it.

  • Shaping the shared design language and system that lets a small team move quickly without the product fragmenting.

  • Partnering with engineering from day one of any problem, not from handoff.

  • Raising the bar for craft — through your own work, through critique, and through the standards you hold the team to.

We think you'll do well here if

  • You've shipped complex software for expert users, in a domain where getting it wrong has real consequences.

  • You design end-to-end and care about the pixels as much as the strategy.

  • You've done serious work on AI or other non-deterministic systems and have opinions about what works and what doesn't.

  • You're comfortable prototyping in code, or motivated to get there.

  • You're direct, kind, and can hold a clear point of view without needing to be the loudest in the room.

  • You want the people who use your product to have better working lives because of it.

You might not enjoy this role if

  • You want to work on a mature product with established patterns. Frontier is early, and the ambiguity is real.

  • You prefer to work handoff-style, away from engineers.

  • You're looking for a role where design sets direction in isolation from product and engineering. We work as one team.

Interview process

  1. Intro call with our talent team (30 min)

  2. Conversation with Duncan, VP of Design (60 min)

  3. Portfolio and case study deep-dive (90 min)

  4. Final conversation with a cross-functional leader (60 min)

Our Recruitment Ethos

We aim to grow the best team - not the most similar one. We know that diversity of individuals fosters diversity of thought, and that strengthens our principle of seeking truth. And we know from experience that diverse teams deliver better work, relevant to the world in which we live. We’re united by a deep intellectual curiosity and desire to use our abilities for measurable positive impact. We strongly encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, ethnicities, genders, religions and sexual orientations.

If you don’t feel you meet all the requirements, but are excited by the role and know you bring some key strengths, please don't hesitate in applying as you might be right for this role, or other roles. We are open to conversations about part-time hours.

A note on AI: we're happy for you to use it for research and interview prep, but please don't use it to generate answers during live interviews. We also use an AI note-taker (Metaview) in interviews so interviewers can stay present (which you can opt out of just let us know,) and every application is reviewed by a human, never decided by AI.

title: Senior Product Manager — Subscriptions (Freemium)
description: Spotify's mission is to unlock the potential of human creativity by giving a million creative artists the opportunity to live off their art and billions of fans the chance to enjoy and be passionate about these creators. The Subscriptions Mission builds and evolves Spotify's subscription products and marketplace experiences to drive sustainable user and revenue growth globally. We focus on helping listeners discover, experience, and unlock the full value of Spotify through awareness, acquisition, activation, retention, and monetization. We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to help shape the future of Spotify's Freemium experience, with a particular focus on India. You'll lead product initiatives that make Premium more compelling, improve the journey from Free to Paid, and create experiences that reflect the needs of local audiences. Working closely with engineering, design, data science, research, marketing, and regional teams, you'll turn consumer insights into meaningful product experiences that drive sustainable subscriber growth. What You'll Do Own the product strategy and roadmap for Spotify's Freemium experience in India, identifying opportunities to grow Free and Premium audiences. Shape how listeners discover, understand, and experience Premium, creating compelling reasons to consider and choose a subscription. Lead the discovery, development, and launch of consumer-facing features, from early ideas and experimentation through rollout and iteration. Design locally relevant Premium experiences and propositions that reflect consumer needs, market dynamics, and different paths to subscription. Develop and run experiments that deepen our understanding of listener behavior, improve conversion, and create lasting value for subscribers. Use funnel, cohort, behavioral, and market insights to identify opportunities, set measurable goals, and prioritize initiatives with the greatest potential impact. Partner with engineering, design, research, marketing, partnerships, and regional teams to bring new experiences to life and adapt successful approaches across markets. Communicate product direction, results, and trade-offs to senior stakeholders, connecting listener experiences with subscriber growth and business outcomes. Who You Are You have a strong track record in product management, bringing consumer-facing products and features to market at scale. You understand what makes a product valuable to consumers and how product experiences, positioning, and perceived value influence willingness to pay. You're experienced in using experimentation, A/B testing, and data analysis to inform product decisions and improve customer experiences. You can translate complex behavioral and market insights into clear product opportunities, priorities, and measurable outcomes. You understand the challenges of building products for diverse audiences and markets, balancing global product consistency with local relevance. You're a thoughtful collaborator who builds strong relationships across product, engineering, design, marketing, research, and regional teams. You're comfortable navigating ambiguity, making informed trade-offs, and adjusting direction as you learn. You communicate clearly, bring different perspectives into decision-making, and help teams align around shared goals. Where You'll Be This role is based in London, UK or Stockholm, Sweden We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home. Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Senior Applied Research Scientist - Personalization
description: The Personalization team makes deciding what to play next easier and more enjoyable for every listener. From Blend to Discover Weekly, we're behind some of Spotify's most-loved features. We built them by understanding the world of music and podcasts better than anyone else. Join us and you'll keep millions of users listening by making great recommendations to each and every one of them. Within Personalization, the Speak Team owns the development of Spotify's state-of-the-art speech models, contributing to speech recognition, speech synthesis, and speech-to-speech models. We craft voice models that match human-level emotional expressiveness, so we can deeply engage our listeners and support creators at scale. Our groundbreaking work on speech synthesis relies on state-of-the-art deep learning methods and evaluation techniques, highly efficient data processing and model serving, and capturing audio of outstanding quality from our voice talent pool. We're looking for a senior applied research scientist with experience in developing novel ML techniques and architectures and with a strong interest in working across a full production pipeline to produce state-of-the-art generative conversational speech-to-speech models. You'll collaborate with our engineering teams to help develop our production pipelines, explore new ideas and methods to improve quality, understanding and realism, as well as push the frontiers of what is possible with our speech technology. What You'll Do Develop and experiment with new methods for speech synthesis and speech recognition, along with end-to-end approaches, building on the latest research and ideas. title: Information Security Engineer - Infrastructure Security
description: A World-Changing Company   Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more. The Role We're looking for an Information Security Engineer who can think broadly about how infrastructure is built, attacked, defended, and improved. You may have deep experience in one area—such as endpoint security, Active Directory, Data Loss Prevention, cloud security, identity, or detection and response—but you’re motivated by solving security problems across the environment. As an Information Security Engineer focused on infrastructure security, you'll help protect Palantir's global endpoints, servers, identity systems, applications, networks, and data flows. You'll work across teams to reduce attack surface, improve defensive controls, investigate security events, and turn security findings into durable architectural and operational improvements. This is not just a corporate security role; the adversaries we face are sophisticated. We need someone who understands both the details and the broader system: how a weakness in one part of the environment can create risk somewhere else, how controls interact, and how to build security improvements that hold up in practice. Core Responsibilities Design, implement, and improve security controls across endpoints, servers, identity systems, cloud services, SaaS applications, networks, and data flows. Drive security posture improvements through hardening standards, configuration management, vulnerability remediation, access controls, monitoring, and ongoing validation. Assess security risks in new platforms, products, architectures, vendors, and services, and turn findings into practical recommendations and engineering work. Build and maintain automation for security operations, including configuration validation, drift monitoring, patching, access reviews, policy enforcement, alert triage, and security hygiene. Partner with Identity, Infrastructure, Engineering, Legal, and other Information Security teams to strengthen security architecture and address recurring risks. Turn insights from assessments, red team exercises, incident investigations, and operational reviews into durable fixes, such as configuration changes, architectural improvements, policy updates, and automation. Build expertise in one or more security domains while contributing across the broader infrastructure security lifecycle. What We're Looking For Experience securing one or more major infrastructure domains, such as Windows, macOS, Linux, Active Directory, cloud platforms, SaaS applications, networking, identity systems, or enterprise endpoints. A broad infrastructure security mindset and curiosity about systems beyond your primary area of expertise. Familiarity with common infrastructure attack paths, adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures, and the controls used to prevent, detect, and contain them. The ability to assess complex environments and recognize how weaknesses across identity, endpoints, applications, networks, cloud services, or data flows can combine to create risk. Experience evaluating security tools and validating that controls are deployed effectively and continue to work as intended. Familiarity with infrastructure-as-code, configuration management, CI/CD, or other approaches to making security controls repeatable and scalable. What We Value The ability to own projects, make progress through ambiguity, and balance competing priorities while working well with colleagues. Experience in complex, high-assurance, regulated, or rapidly changing environments. Comfort moving between strategic problem-solving and hands-on technical work. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical risks and work with partner teams to drive remediation. Contributions to security programs, tooling, automation, incident investigations, or technical research—whether public or internal. What We Require 5+ years of hands-on experience in information security, infrastructure security, security engineering, security operations, or a closely related field. Demonstrated experience securing at least one major infrastructure or security domain, with the ability and interest to work across multiple domains. Active TS/SCI security clearance, or eligibility and willingness to obtain one. A strong sense of ownership, sound judgment, and integrity. Life at Palantir   We want every Palantirian to achieve their best outcomes, that’s why we celebrate individuals’ strengths, skills, and interests, from your first interview to your longterm growth, rather than rely on traditional career ladders. Paying attention to the needs of our community enables us to optimize our opportunities to grow and helps ensure many pathways to success at Palantir. Promoting health and well-being across all areas of Palantirians’ lives is just one of the ways we’re investing in our community. Learn more at Life at Palantir and note that our offerings may vary by region.   In keeping consistent with Palantir’s values and culture, we believe employees are “better together” and in-person work affords the opportunity for more creative outcomes. Therefore, we encourage employees to work from our offices to foster connectivity and innovation. Many teams do offer hybrid options (WFH a day or two a week), allowing our employees to strike the right trade-off for their personal productivity. Based on business need, there are a few roles that allow for “Remote” work on an exceptional basis. If you are applying for one of these roles, you must work from the city and or country in which you are employed. If the posting is specified as Onsite, you are required to work from an office.   If you want to empower the world's most important institutions, you belong here. Palantir values excellence regardless of background. We are committed to making the application and hiring process accessible to everyone and will provide a reasonable accommodation for those living with a disability. If you need an accommodation for the application or hiring process , please and let us know how we can help.   Please note that you will never be asked to submit a payment or share financial information to participate in our interview process. If you suspect that you've been contacted by a scammer, we recommend you cease all communication with the individual and consider reporting them to the relevant authorities, such as the US FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) . About the role

Storio Group produces millions of personalised photo products every year across brands like Photobox, Hofmann, and Albelli. Our business is highly seasonal and promotional, and planning is how we stay ahead of it. Everything we sell is made to order. We turn sales data and commercial insight into forecasts of sales, volume and ASP that give the business sales and margin visibility and drive stock and production capacity decisions across Europe.

 

As Senior Demand & Merchandise Planner, you will be a core Subject Matter Expert in our rapidly developing S&OP function. Reporting to the Head of Demand Planning, you will bridge top-line commercial forecasts with item-level operational reality. You will validate B2C category sales, volume and ASP forecasts, own the sub-category and item mix beneath them, establish B2B forecasting, and improve forecast phasing across our peak cycles. This is a high-impact role where you will build quality into our planning process and support commercial and operational readiness.




How you embrace curiosity daily

Make your mark by taking on these core day-to-day responsibilities:

  • Validate and check Commercial & Marketing's monthly, weekly, and daily category top-line forecasts of sales, volume and ASP against run rates, promotional plans, and customer strategies

  • Challenge forecast assumptions constructively across key markets and products, including mix and ASP shifts, when inputs diverge from historical trends or operational reality

  • Own the detailed item planning process, splitting category forecasts into granular sub-category and item variant forecasts across sales, volume and ASP, providing item sales mix and margin visibility, and Operations with accurate production requirements

  • Decompose forecasts into their parts (baseline, commercial initiatives and new products), so each can be challenged and tracked

  • Drive continuous improvement in weekly and daily forecast phasing, reviewing and validating sales forecasts against promotional mechanics, seasonal uplift spikes, and Last Order Dates for key gifting events

  • Build pragmatic models and tools that help forecast owners submit higher-quality phasing inputs

  • Take end-to-end ownership of forecasting for B2B vendors, integrating these streams into the central S&OP process


    • How you make your mark

    In this role, you will deliver real impact across our commercial and supply chain objectives


  • Support robust commercial consensus by bringing planning expertise to cross-functional partners

  • Validate and check promotional phasing directly to Last Order Dates to improve peak season operational readiness

  • Provide sales, volume, ASP and margin visibility through accurate, granular item forecasts aligned to category forecasts from Commercial & Marketing

  • Close unforecasted blind spots by building baseline forecasts for B2B channels

  • Prepare variance analysis and scenario reporting packs for monthly demand review meetings

  • Partner with Supply Planning so item-level forecast changes translate smoothly into capacity planning

  • Identify opportunities to refine planning spreadsheets and models to remove manual friction and improve data integrity


    • What you bring to the team

  • Demand Planning, Merchandise Planning or Merchandising experience in a fast-paced environment like Retail, E-Commerce or FMCG

  • Experience forecasting sales value and ASP, not just volume, and using category and product mix to give margin visibility

  • Proven track record of managing item-level planning, category and product mix modelling, and promotional uplift analysis

  • Hands-on experience challenging commercial, trading or marketing teams on forecast assumptions using clear data

  • Advanced MS Excel or Google Sheets data modelling skills with complex multi-category and multi-country datasets

  • Strong commercial mindset with the ability to manage defined processes independently

  • Practical problem-solving approach that favours workable tools over complex theoretical models


    • What sets you apart

  • Career experience with exposure to adjacent functions like Supply Planning, Trading, Marketing, or Finance

  • Background in seasonal, promotion-led, high-volume direct-to-consumer or multi-market businesses, along with experience using Demand or Merchandise Planning systems

  • Relevant formal education or degree in business, supply chain, or a related analytical field

    • Why Storio? 

    You will join a function that is investing in its planning capability and has the scale to make your work genuinely matter — millions of orders, dozens of markets, seasonal peaks that test every part of the supply chain. You will have a clear scope, a supportive manager, and real opportunity to grow your expertise within a business that takes supply chain seriously.

    No two months look the same.

    If you want to build your demand planning career in a business where accuracy has real consequences and planning as a concept is step-changing every year, we’d love to hear from you.

    At Storio Group, we help people hold onto life's moments. We make personalised photo products that turn fleeting memories into things you can keep, share, and re-live.

description: <div class="content-intro"><p>At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.</p></div><p>We are seeking a highly motivated and analytical individual to join our Growth Analytics International team. This team plays a crucial role in conducting research, monitoring performance, and running experiments to develop exceptional products for both consumers and merchants while driving long-term growth for the business. As Affirm continues expanding into new international markets, this role will be instrumental in establishing the operational analytics framework for new launches, beginning with Australia and expanding into future international markets. The ideal candidate will possess strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, a collaborative mindset, an eagerness to learn, and the patience to tackle complex challenges.</p> <p>Our team takes an end-to-end business analytics perspective, partnering across the organization to develop recommendations and solutions that enable the business to successfully execute its growth and profitability strategies. This role requires someone who can combine analytical rigor with business acumen to influence decisions and drive measurable outcomes.</p> <p><strong>What you’ll do</strong></p> <ul> <li>Establish and evolve the operational analytics framework for new international markets, ensuring scalable measurement, reporting, and decision-making capabilities as we expand globally.</li> <li>Operate with a business owner mindset by proactively identifying opportunities through analysis and product sense to enhance user experience, growth, and profitability.</li> <li>Own business problems from end to end by translating analytical insights into recommendations and optimization strategies that support business growth, profitability, and operational excellence.</li> <li>Take ownership of the end-to-end analytics process: define success metrics, generate insights and hypotheses, track performance, and create intuitive dashboards and reports that can be easily shared across the organization. Develop scalable analytics solutions and data models.</li> <li>Tackle ambiguous problems by identifying the core hypotheses and designing actionable experiments to validate product-market fit and economic viability.</li> <li>Translate analytical findings into clear and compelling narratives and business cases for leadership to inform decision-making.</li> <li>Spearhead weekly cross-functional metric reviews, collaborating with partners to conduct deep dives into significant metric shifts and suggest actionable steps.</li> <li>Partner effectively across Product, Risk, Finance, Commercial, and Operations to align strategies and execute against business objectives.</li> <li>Foster strong cross-functional relationships and establish yourself as a trusted advisor to team members.</li> <li>Mentor and guide junior analysts to deliver high-impact work that drives business results.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What we look for:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Passion to redefine the lending and financial industry for the better.</li> <li>Strong understanding of the consumer lending and credit industry, including lending economics, portfolio performance, and credit metrics. Experience supporting international lending markets, particularly Europe and/or APAC, is highly desirable.</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to balance growth objectives with profitability and develop data-driven growth strategies.</li> <li>Bachelor's or Master's degree in a quantitatively rigorous subject area such as statistics, mathematics, finance, or economics.</li> <li>5+ years of proven success in a cross-functional analytical role.</li> <li>Practical and theoretical knowledge of A/B testing.</li> <li>Experience with SQL and performing statistical analysis using Python.</li> <li>Experience simultaneously balancing multiple workstreams and prioritizing an analytics roadmap.</li> <li>Demonstrated curiosity and a growth mindset, with hands-on experience using AI-powered tools such as Cursor, Claude, or similar assistants to accelerate analysis, automate workflows, enhance problem-solving, and advocate for AI adoption across analytical workflows.</li> <li>Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to influence both technical and non-technical audiences.</li> <li>Comfortable partnering across multiple cross-functional teams, particularly Product, Risk, Commercial, Finance, and Operations.</li> <li>Ability to think creatively and critically while thriving in a fast-paced, dynamic, and often ambiguous work environment.</li> <li>Willingness to go out of your way to help teammates, with humility and a team-first mindset.</li> <li>Previous experience mentoring and guiding junior analysts.</li> </ul> <h4><strong>Compensation &amp; Benefits</strong></h4> <p><strong>Pay Grade</strong> - M<br><strong>Equity Grade</strong> - 5<br><br>Employees new to Affirm typically come in <strong>at the start of the pay range</strong>. Affirm focuses on providing a simple and transparent pay structure which is based on a variety of factors, including location, experience and job-related skills.&nbsp;<br><br>Base pay is part of a total compensation package that may include monthly stipends for health, wellness and tech spending, and benefits (including 100% subsidized medical coverage, dental and vision for you and your dependents). In addition, the employees may be eligible for equity rewards offered by Affirm Holdings, Inc. (parent company).<br><br>GBR base pay range per year: <strong>£113,000 - £161,000 &nbsp;<br></strong><br>Location - <strong>Remote UK</strong></p> <p>#LI-Remote</p><div class="content-conclusion"><div> <p><strong>Remote-first with flexibility built in</strong><strong><br></strong>Affirm is proud to be a remote-first company. Most roles can be done from almost anywhere within the country of employment. title: Research Scientist – Foundation Models and Multimodal AI
description: About us Owkin is an agentic AI company pioneering Biological Artificial Superintelligence to solve problems in biology where human researchers alone have failed. Owkin builds K Pro - an AI scientist for pharmaceutical research and strategic decision-making. K Pro orchestrates a suite of AI skills and tools to decode complex biology, accelerate research, and dramatically increase productivity. K Pro is built on Owkin’s unrivalled multimodal patient data network, state-of-the-art AI for biology and a decade of experience working with pharmaceutical partners. Position is based in our Paris office or remotely in France, UK, Germany. Please submit your CV in English About the role: We are seeking a driven Research Scientist with hands-on expertise in Foundation Models (FMs) and Multimodal AI to help drive the next phase of our machine learning platform. In this role, you will bridge cutting-edge AI research and practical application. Rather than training massive base models from scratch, your focus will be on fine-tuning, adapting, and aligning open-weights foundation models across diverse data modalities (e.g. structured tabular data, single-cell scRNA-seq, image representations, and natural language) to build multimodal systems. In particular, you will be responsible for: Model adaptation and optimization: Adapt, fine-tune, and evaluate state-of-the-art open-source foundation models (e.g., domain-specific transformers, vision-language models) using fine-tuning and transfer learning strategies. Multimodal integration: Design and implement cross-modal alignment architectures (e.g., contrastive learning, projection heads, unified embedding spaces) to fuse structured, sequential, and text/image data layers. Pipeline and evaluation engineering: Build rigorous, domain-tailored benchmarking frameworks and evaluation pipelines to validate model reliability, generalization, and downstream task performance. Applied R&D collaboration: Work closely with cross-functional teams (data engineers, domain specialists, and software engineers) to integrate adapted models into scalable production and inference workflows. Low-hanging fruit innovation: Identify high-impact, incremental improvements in data pre-processing, embedding representation, and fine-tuning to maximize model performance without unnecessary computational overhead. About you Required qualifications / experience: Education: Ph.D. or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Mathematics or a related quantitative field. Experience: 2-4 years of post-degree experience applying deep learning and foundation models to complex datasets. Foundation models: Demonstrated experience adapting and fine-tuning foundation models. Multimodal learning: Proven experience with cross-modal representation learning, joint embedding alignment (e.g., CLIP-style architectures), or vision-language models. Technical stack: Advanced proficiency in Python and modern deep learning frameworks ( PyTorch , Hugging Face ecosystem). Hands-on experience with fine-tuning techniques. Familiarity with data engineering tools for handling large-scale or multi-modal datasets (Parquet, AnnData, HDF5). Preferred qualifications/bonus: Experience working with biological or omics data (e.g., scRNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics, clinical and/or histology data). Experience deploying or scaling models using containerized environments (Docker, Kubernetes) and cloud infrastructure (AWS/GCP). Track record of open-source contributions or peer-reviewed publications at top ML conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR) or domain-specific journals. #LI-HB1 What we offer Flexible work organization Friendly and informal working environment Opportunity to work with an international team with high technical and scientific backgrounds Recruitment Process & Security Please complete the form and submit your CV. Owkin is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, sex, gender, sexual orientation, age, color, religion, national origin, protected veteran status or on the basis of disability. Owkin is a great place to work. As a coveted workplace we are, unfortunately, vulnerable to recruitment phishing scams. We urge all job seekers and candidates to be wary of potential scams. Most of these have individuals posing as representatives of prominent companies, including Owkin, with the aim of obtaining personal, sensitive, or financial information from applicants. These scams prey upon an individual’s desire to obtain a job and can sometimes “feel” like a genuine recruitment process. Some red flags are identified below. Should you encounter a recruitment process that claims to be for Owkin but is not consistent with the below, please do not provide any personal or financial information: Legitimate Owkin recruitment processes include communication with candidates through recognized professional networks, such as LinkedIn. Communication is always through an official Owkin email address (from the @ owkin.com domain), over the phone or through our applicant tracking system (Ashby). The Owkin talent team do use platforms such as LinkedIn, however if you have any concern or doubt about this contact, please ask for them to send an email from @ Owkin.com . The Owkin talent team will not solicit personal data from candidates during the application phase including, but not limited to, date of birth, social security numbers, or bank account information; Legitimate Owkin interviews may be conducted over the phone, in person, or via an approved enterprise videoconferencing service (Google Meets). Offers will be extended both verbally and in written format. title: Cdi - Charge(E) De Sourcing Et Developpement Textile Senior (H/F)
description: LA MAISON JACQUEMUS Jacquemus a été fondée par Simon Porte Jacquemus en 2009 à Paris, en France. Dédiée à la mémoire de la mère du créateur, la marque puise son inspiration dans une passion pour la culture. Les collections femme et homme font référence à l'art de vivre à la française et aux gestes universels de beauté, intégrant des influences allant de la photographie d'art aux arts décoratifs, en passant par le cinéma, la peinture et la sculpture. Au fil des années, Jacquemus a mis en scène ses défilés dans des lieux uniques et inattendus, notamment une piscine parisienne, le Musée Picasso, un champ de lavande en Provence, un champ de blé aux abords de Paris, un marais salant en Camargue et une plage à Hawaï. Plus récemment, la marque a investi des lieux tels que le canal du Château de Versailles (Le Chouchou), la Fondation Maeght (Les Sculptures), la Casa Malaparte (La Casa) et l'appartement parisien d'Auguste Perret (La Croisière). Basé dans le 8ᵉ arrondissement de Paris, Jacquemus est une maison de mode indépendante comptant plus de 300 employés. Réputée pour sa forte présence numérique et son expansion internationale, la marque a développé des expériences de vente innovantes à travers le monde avant d'ouvrir son premier flagship permanent au 58 Avenue Montaigne à Paris en 2022. Depuis, des boutiques ont été ouvertes à New York (SoHo) et Londres (New Bond Street). VOTRE ROLE Rattaché(e) à la Responsable Tissus, le/la Chargé(e) de Sourcing et Développement Textile Senior assure le sourcing et le développement des matières textiles pour les collections de prêt-à-porter Homme et Femme JACQUEMUS. Grâce à son expertise textile, sa sensibilité produit et sa connaissance du marché, elle/il identifie les matières adaptées à la vision créative de la Maison et accompagne leur développement jusqu’à leur transmission aux équipes Achats. VOS MISSIONS 1. Sourcing textile Rechercher et sourcer les matières en accord avec les besoins des collections. Présenter régulièrement les sélections à la Responsable Tissus et aux équipes Design. Préparer et animer les rendez-vous fournisseurs. Participer aux salons textiles à Paris et à Milan. Assurer la gestion et l’organisation de la tissuthèque. 2. Développement textile Lancer et suivre les développements textiles : lab dips, impressions, jacquards et développements spécifiques. Assurer le suivi avec les fournisseurs et les techniciens des usines textiles. Garantir le respect des délais et des priorités de développement. Organiser la passation des développements à la Chargée des Achats Tissus. Assurer l’archivage et la traçabilité des développements. 3. Coordination et pilotage Élaborer et suivre le planning de sourcing et de développement avec les équipes. Vérifier les racks et les boards tissus avec la Chargée des Achats Tissus. Réaliser un point hebdomadaire avec les équipes Design et les Chefs de Produit. Contribuer à la mise en place du plan de collection matières et au suivi de son cadrage. Suivre le budget de développement textile. VOTRE PROFIL Minimum 4 ans d’expérience en sourcing et développement textile. Expertise des matières et bonne connaissance des fournisseurs et techniciens textiles. Forte sensibilité produit et intérêt marqué pour l’univers du textile. Curiosité, proactivité et sens des priorités. Maîtrise de l’anglais ; l’italien est un plus. Find Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

About the Project 

Project Hydrus is a scripted and conversational audio data collection project. The recordings produced help build natural, everyday-sounding synthesized voices for conversational AI products — voices that sound like real people talking, not scripted performances. 

As Session Director, you'll lead live recording sessions with Voice Contributors, guiding them through scripted scenarios to produce natural, conversational-quality audio. This hands-on role blends creative direction, coaching, and technical audio judgment — making scripted material sound authentic and unscripted, rather than recited, while keeping sessions moving at a natural pace. 

What You'll Do 

    - Direct voice performers through scripted scenarios, coaching for natural, conversational delivery rather than verbatim recitation. 

    - Build quick scene context for performers (who, where, why) and improvise to fill narrative or dialogue gaps live, keeping sessions flowing naturally. 

    - Adapt scripted wording for natural phrasing and regional/dialect authenticity as needed. 

    - Monitor and correct technical audio quality in real time: mic technique, pacing, clarity, and background noise. 

    - Manage session pacing to meet recording targets without sacrificing performance quality, and maintain organized notes on adjustments and retakes. 

    - Create a supportive, low-pressure environment for performers, including those with limited prior voice experience. 

What We're Looking For 

Required 

    - Native fluency in the required language (with specific dialect), with a strong ear for natural, colloquial phrasing. 

    - Experience directing, coaching, or producing voice or audio talent (e.g., voice direction, casting direction, audio/podcast production, dubbing/ADR, or theater direction). 

    - Demonstrated ability to give clear, specific, actionable performance direction. 

    - Strong working knowledge of basic recording/mic technique (proximity, plosives, room noise, levels). 

    - Comfortable improvising and adjusting scripted material on the spot. 

    - Excellent interpersonal skills; able to build rapport quickly with performers of varying experience levels. 

Preferred (nice to have, not required) 

    - Background in improv, theater direction, or acting coaching. 

    - Experience directing non-professional or first-time voice talent specifically. 

    - Familiarity with DAWs or recording software (e.g., Pro Tools, Adobe Audition, Reaper) for spot-checking audio quality.

Commitment & Compensation

title: Senior Manager, Integrated MarComms, France & Benelux
description: Tinder exists to help people meet, connect and create a spark. After 13 years of leadership in the dating industry, culture is what keeps that mission relevant to each new generation of daters. Product is central to this shift. Every new feature is a chance to tell a human story about how people connect, and culture is where those stories land. To make that shift real, we’re bringing our Tinder MarComms regional EMEA strategy together: one unified in-country team in each key market and one regional structure. Communications now sits within Marketing, so both work toward the same KPIs and growth objectives. The Integrated MarComms role is where culture meets brand relevance, with one holistic objective: driving MAU growth. Social Media is the true D2C MarComms engine for Tinder, and creator and influencer led activations play a central role in driving registrations, reactivations and cultural relevance. The regional MarComms team owns the full paid, earned and owned media cycle across key markets. The Integrated MarComms Senior Manager leads the earned and influence dimension of that ecosystem, with a strong influence on owned social channels and brand partnership storytelling. The role reports to the Director of Marketing of France & Benelux. It works in a matrix with the Snr. Director of Social Media, Snr. Manager of Brand Partnerships, and closely with the Global Comms team.   Key Responsibilities 1. Creator & Influencer Ecosystem Engagement Build and nurture a diverse network of community voices: creators, influencers, podcast hosts, cultural commentators and community leaders. Develop collaborations rooted in a strong audience insight and shared creative idea, giving partners a meaningful role beyond content distribution. Work closely with social, influence and brand partnership teams to connect local opportunities with broader brand priorities. Create opportunities for audiences to participate and share their own stories, turning campaigns into conversations that extend beyond launch. 2. Social-First Integrated MarComms Strategy Translate market priorities into integrated MarComms plans for France & Benelux, in close partnership with the market lead, marketing manager and EMEA teams. Develop compelling creative ideas with the potential to travel across paid, owned and earned channels, giving each channel a clear role in building relevance, consideration and action. Build strategies around how Gen Z discovers, shares and participates in culture, across various formats, creators, podcasts, digital communities and emerging platforms. Help raise the creative and strategic standard of Tinder’s organic social channels, building distinctive formats and stories that audiences want to be part of. 3. Creating Cultural Narratives for Gen Z Turn audience insights, cultural tensions and dating behaviours into locally relevant narratives that strengthen Tinder’s role in modern dating, particularly among young women. Make product innovation meaningful through human stories and creative experiences that show how Tinder helps people meet, connect and create a spark. Broaden the representation of dating success to reflect the connections, experiences and stories Gen Z values, building a more positive and credible perception of Tinder. Anticipate cultural moments and emerging conversations, using data, cultural understanding and creative judgment to identify where the brand can make a meaningful contribution. Own a quarterly and annual activation calendar, balancing planned campaigns with timely opportunities, and contribute local insights and ideas to EMEA initiatives. 4. Earned Impact & Measurement Connect MarComms activity to clear objectives, supporting registrations and reactivations as contributions to the overarching goal of MAU growth. Own measurement of earned and social impact, including share of conversation, message uptake, sentiment and meaningful engagement, moving beyond coverage volume and impressions. Partner with Insights and Analytics to assess contributions to brand consideration, trust, relevance and perceptions of the dating experiences Tinder enables. Use results to sharpen creative choices, improve distribution and recommend where to scale, adapt or stop activity. 5. End-to-End Campaign & Agency Management Own campaigns from brief to launch to wrap-up in France & Benelux, making sure paid, owned and earned moments work as one story. Brief, steer and hold agency partners to the bar on creative quality, timelines and budgets, so their work feeds the integrated plan. Keep workflows with EMEA and Global teams clear, so local executions stay on brand and on time. Coordinate crisis and issue management with Comms leadership, anticipating sensitive topics and keeping responses fast, aligned and on brand. As part of our team, you'll enjoy: The hustle of a startup with the impact of a global business Tremendous opportunity to solve some of the industry’s most exciting problems Working with an extraordinary team of smart, creative, fun and highly motivated people Comprehensive health coverage, competitive pay, team bonding events, yoga classes and social events Commitment to Inclusion At Tinder, we don’t just accept difference, we celebrate it. We strive to build a workplace that reflects the rich diversity of our members around the world, and we value unique perspectives and backgrounds. Even if you don’t meet all the listed qualifications, we invite you to apply and show us how your skills could transfer. Tinder is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace where we welcome people of all sexes, gender identities, races, ethnicities, disabilities, and other lived experiences. Learn more here: https://www.lifeattinder.com/dei If you require reasonable accommodation to complete a job application, pre-employment testing, or a job interview or to otherwise participate in the hiring process, please speak to your Talent Acquisition Partner directly.   #Tinder Find Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

title: Stage Data Analyst / Support Applicatifs Finance & Innovation (H/F/X) - Lyon
description: Handicap International (HI) est une association de solidarité internationale indépendante et impartiale, qui intervient dans les situations de pauvreté et d’exclusion, de conflits et de catastrophes. Œuvrant aux côtés des personnes handicapées et vulnérabilisées, elle agit et témoigne pour répondre à leurs besoins essentiels et améliorer leurs conditions de vie. Elle s’engage à promouvoir le respect de leur dignité et de leurs droits fondamentaux. Depuis sa création en 1982, HI a mis en place des programmes de développement dans plus de 59 pays et intervient dans de nombreuses situations d’urgence. Aujourd'hui, nous avons 4000 employés dans le monde. Chez Handicap International, nous croyons fermement en l'importance de l'inclusion et de la diversité au sein de notre structure. C'est pourquoi nous sommes engagés dans une politique handicap afin de favoriser l'accueil et l'intégration de personnes en situation de handicap. Merci d’indiquer si vous avez besoin d’un aménagement particulier, y compris pour participer aux premiers entretiens. Au sein du Pôle Support Formations & Projets, le stagiaire contribuera à l'amélioration continue des outils, processus et données utilisés par les équipes Finance.  Dans un environnement mêlant support applicatif, gestion de la donnée, amélioration des processus et innovation digitale, il participera à plusieurs projets visant à renforcer l'efficacité opérationnelle des utilisateurs et à développer la qualité des services rendus aux métiers.   Ce stage vise à : ·       Améliorer la qualité et la disponibilité de la documentation applicative. ·       Renforcer la capitalisation des connaissances liées au support utilisateur. ·       Contribuer à l'amélioration de la qualité des données financières et opérationnelles. ·       Participer à l'automatisation de traitements et à l'optimisation des outils existants. ·       Développer des indicateurs de pilotage du support et de l'activité. ·       Explorer les opportunités offertes par l'intelligence artificielle et les outils Microsoft pour les métiers de la Finance. ·       Contribuer à la conception de solutions innovantes facilitant l'assistance aux utilisateurs  Dans ce cadre, vos missions seront les suivantes : Innovation et Intelligence Artificielle Explorer les usages de l'IA appliqués au support et aux métiers Finance. Participer à la conception de solutions innovantes s'appuyant sur les agents IA, la gestion des connaissances et l'automatisation des processus. Contribuer à des expérimentations autour de l'assistance aux utilisateurs, de la formation et de l'intégration des nouveaux collaborateurs. Support applicatif et amélioration continue Participer à l'analyse et au traitement des demandes utilisateurs. Contribuer à la capitalisation des solutions et bonnes pratiques. Identifier des pistes d'amélioration pour renforcer la qualité de service et la stabilité des applications. Chez Handicap International, nous croyons fermement en l'importance de l'inclusion et de la diversité au sein de notre structure. C'est pourquoi nous sommes engagés dans une politique handicap afin de favoriser l'accueil et l'intégration de personnes en situation de handicap.

Dans ce cadre, vos missions seront les suivantes :

Innovation et Intelligence Artificielle

About Voodoo

Voodoo is a consumer tech company founded in Paris in 2013, with one mission: entertain the world. Today we are 1,000+ people, generating $1b+ in annual revenue, profitably. Our games and apps have passed 8 billion downloads and reach 200 million+ active users every month, making Voodoo the #3 mobile publisher worldwide in downloads, after Google and Meta. We were backed by Goldman Sachs, Tencent and GBL along the way.

Team

Our Growth team is a transversal entity aiming to scale any product we build. It combines user acquisition, creative content production, monetization, and the tech capabilities required to turn applications into global hits. With over 150 experts, we operate at the forefront of mobile marketing and ad tech.

Today, our Creative team makes 10K+ ads a month, mostly by hand. We are rebuilding that process with AI to multiply both our output and our hit rate. The challenge is to build tools that produce at massive scale, with quality that holds up.

Role

You build the AI tools that let our creative team scale ads production without losing what makes them great. You sit with the people who use your tools every day, understand how they work and ship fast. AI brings speed and scale; taste and context stay human and your tools free our creatives to focus on exactly that.

Your scope covers tooling for video and playable ads production:

  • Work hand in hand with Creative Strategists, AI Content Producers and Marketing Developers to turn their recurring tasks into tools

  • Track how your tools are used and what they change in production volume and ad performance, then iterate

  • Keep watching new AI models (image, video, agents) and bring the useful ones into our pipeline

Profile

  • You graduated from a top engineering program, or you have up to 3 years of experience building internal tools, ideally with AI

  • You are at ease with LLMs, agentic workflows and generative AI for image and video

  • You keep a close eye on new AI models

  • You speak and write English fluently

américain.</li> <li>Représenter Vast lors d'événements de l'industrie spatiale, aérospatiale et de défense internationale en Europe, au Moyen-Orient et en Asie.</li> <li>Faire des présentations, title: CENTRALE LYON - Post-doctoral researcher (12 months) Mathematics of energy-efficient AI: diffusion models on emerging hardware
description: The question Generating one image with a diffusion model means evaluating a large neural network tens to hundreds of times. That repetition is where the energy goes, and it is part of why data-centre demand is now visible at grid scale: the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory puts US data-centre electricity use at 176 TWh in 2023, 4.4 % of national consumption, a figure that more than doubled since 2017 largely because of AI servers, and projects 325–580 TWh by 2028. Emerging hardware attacks exactly this primitive: analog in-memory computing, silicon photonics, ferroelectric devices and stochastic computing perform the underlying matrix–vector products at lower energy than digital CMOS, under conditions on scale and precision, but return a perturbed result. The usual objection is that nobody can say in advance how much perturbation a model tolerates. In EMMA, this opportunity is pursued through a PCM-based photonic matrix–vector engine as the primary demonstrator, complemented where appropriate by FeFET-based analog computing, so that device-level non-idealities are treated as explicit design parameters rather than as after-the-fact implementation losses. Diffusion models are an unusual case in which that question has a mathematical answer: their convergence theory bounds the discrepancy between the generated and target distributions by three terms, of which only one, the L 2 error of the learned score, depends on the hardware. That side is now in good shape: for stochastic samplers, bounds linear in the dimension under minimal assumptions on the data; for deterministic samplers, a matching theory under regularity. What is missing is the bridge. The theory is parameterised by a score error, the hardware literature by conductance noise, effective number of bits and photons per multiply–accumulate; nobody has written the map between them, in either direction. The quantisation literature for diffusion models reports image-quality scores; the induced L 2 score error, in the form the convergence theory needs, is directly measurable and goes unreported. One open sub-question sets the direction: the distinction between an error redrawn at each evaluation, as in stochastic computing, and an error frozen at write time, as in deterministic quantisation, has been settled in one setting only, and not the one hardware lives in; carrying it over is what this position exists to do. The work is judged on one concrete outcome. For at least one architecture, we want to show that theenergy gain from moving the score evaluation off digital CMOS is real, measured where it survives integration and not extrapolated from a single tile, and that it is paid for by a loss in sample quality that is small and, above all, tunable: a knob the designer sets, whose position the theory predicts rather than discovers afterwards. What you will do The work is organised in four packages, summarised below; the full research programme is available from the supervisors on request. 1. Make the score error measurable, starting from Gaussian targets where the whole error decomposition is closed-form. You will report the induced score error for a given perturbation of the network’s arithmetic, the number the theory needs and the quantisation literature does not report. 2. Map device physics onto the theory. Propagate the published error models for the technologies INL works on through the score network into an explicit score-error budget, separating what is proved from what is measured. 3. Extend the guarantees. Existing bounds assume a deterministic oracle, or a benign randomised one; extend them to error that is part frozen at write time and part redrawn at each call, and settle, on the way, which process the score error should be controlled along. 4. Co-design with INL, and deliver the proof of concept. Turn the score-error budget into an energy– accuracy frontier for INL’s PCM-based photonic matrix–vector engine, using device-calibrated circuitlevel models; a FeFET-based analog alternative may be considered where appropriate. Jointly vary sampler steps, stochastic bitstream length and effective precision to identify an operating point predicted to yield a real energy advantage over digital CMOS at a small, tunable loss in sample quality. The result is a frontier predicted from mathematical and hardware models, then verified against calibrated measurements. A clear negative answer is more useful to us than a vague positive one: a negative result on point 3 leaves points 1 and 2 intact and turns point 4 from a prediction into a measurement. Who we are looking for Required • A PhD in applied mathematics, statistics, machine learning, electronic engineering, computer science or a closely related field, obtained (or with the defence scheduled) before the start of the contract. • A strong foundation in probability and stochastic analysis, numerical analysis, optimisation, or machine learning: SDEs, Girsanov’s theorem, time reversal of diffusions, with the ability to apply it rigorously to diffusion or other generative models. • Familiarity with the convergence theory of sampling algorithms, or the demonstrated capacity to acquire it quickly, for example through Langevin/MCMC analysis, optimal transport or concentration of measure. • Solid scientific computing (PyTorch or JAX), and the habit of writing code others can run. Ability and motivation to work across mathematical modelling and hardware-aware AI. • Working English; French is not required. Valued, not required Prior work on diffusion or score-based generative models; numerical analysis of finite-precision arithmetic. Familiarity with hardware-aware machine learning, approximate or stochastic computing, analogue in-memory computing, device modelling, circuit simulation, photonics, ferroelectric devices, or energy modelling. Experience linking model accuracy or robustness to implementation non-idealities, such as quantisation, noise, drift, variability, finite precision, or correlated errors. Evidence of interdisciplinary research, for example work at the interface of mathematics, machine learning, devices, circuits, architectures, or electronic-design automation. No hardware experience is expected or needed to apply. What matters most We are seeking a researcher who wants to explore how to turn physical constraints into mathematical and architectural design parameters. The project does not require prior laboratory hardware experience: INL provides device expertise, measured characteristics and modelling infrastructure. However, the successful candidate must be prepared to engage critically with non-ideal analog, photonic and ferroelectric accelerators, and to work with both supervisors to connect device-level error mechanisms, score-error guarantees and the energy–quality trade-off of diffusion-model inference. Candidates with a primarily mathematical background and strong curiosity for hardware are welcome, as are candidates from AIhardware, device-modeling, circuit, architecture or EDA backgrounds who have the stochastic-analysis maturity needed to develop the theory. The decisive criterion is the ability to make the mathematics and hardware inform one another, producing predictions that are quantitative, testable and relevant to an energy-efficient accelerator demonstrator. What we offer • A real double supervision, with weekly meetings that alternate between ICJ and INL. The two laboratories are on the same campus, five minutes apart on foot. • A question publishable on both sides: mathematics journals for the theory, design and hardware venues for the co-design. • Involvement in INL’s design–technology co-optimisation work through the PEPR Électronique CHOOSE project, and contact with the group’s ferroelectric and photonic device work (FVLLMONTI, Ferro4EdgeAI). • Support for conference travel and open-access publication, funded by the two host laboratories, and the career-development measures the establishment provides for post-doctoral researchers. • Practical help for international recruits through Espace ULYS, the EURAXESS service centre for Université de Lyon: visas, housing, health cover, banking, schooling. Conditions Twelve-month fixed-term contract under French public law, full time (1 607 h annual reference), 25 working days of annual leave plus the RTT days of the establishment’s scheme. Affiliation to the régime général for health and to IRCANTEC for supplementary pension; employer contribution to complementary health cover under the scheme in force at the establishment; 75 % reimbursement of publictransport season tickets, up to the statutory ceiling. The exact number of RTT days is set by the establishment. Find more English Speaking Jobs in France on Arbeitnow
